summary: Both paragraphs are mostly faithful, but each has errors that change the sense or the framing. In 3:7 the Kabbalist named by וז"ל is the speaker and stands outside the quotation, and בעל היכל הברכה is the author of a book (Heikhal ha-Berakhah, transliterated); וז"ל of 3:7.94 was dropped, אף שמדבר mistranslated, and Song 5:12 and Deut 17:6 unlisted. In 3:8, עמדו ולא ענו עוד is Job 32:16 (plural: 'they stood and answered no more'), 'the Shekhinah of our strength' was made an apposition, 'or whispers' reversed the subject, and several punctuation and capital faults need correcting; Job 20:26, 1 Kgs 18:17 and Deut 13:6 are added to apparatus. The Aramaic source of the maiden without eyes is rightly left unnamed (decisions: no unreferenced sources); Da'at is correctly transliterated; כ' = כתב is confirmed. Open questions: וכ' (3:7.87) as וכו', the 'idly' of Lev 19:16, and the כ of כשומע כעונה כמדבר.

patches.value: §7. And these are the words of the Kabbalist, the author of Heikhal ha-Berakhah: "A positive commandment on the court to inquire into and to examine the witnesses with seven inquiries, etc. There are also examinations, which are questions: what clothing he wore; the dust of the ground on which he stood, whether black, or sand, or clay; and if they contradict one another, the testimony is void. From the roots of this commandment: the included bride, the beautiful young maiden who has no eyes, the governance of this world, that there be free choice, whose eyes are like doves, a deception to the sons of man. Her eyes in the Palace of Merit: the eyes of the congregation, who judge with knowledge on the testimony of two witnesses, two crowns; and the Da'at is the secret of the eyes, as is known; and this light spreads in seven aspects, etc." See there. And concerning the commandment "You shall not go about as a talebearer," he wrote, and these are his words: " that one should not tell his fellow that his adversary has spoken evil about him, as it is said, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.' And among the laws of the commandment: even though he speaks the truth, there is a great sin in this. And also within the scope of this prohibition: that one should not speak in disparagement of his fellow, even if true, and this is as if he denied the fundamental principle, etc." And he expanded further on the punishment of the one who tells slander and on the reward of the one who guards from it; see there.
patches.reason: Three faults. (1) וז"ל followed by a name is 'and these are the words of X:' (decisions: וז"ל הזהר), so the Kabbalist is the named speaker and stands outside the opening quotation mark; the translation put him inside the quotation and rendered 'his words' with no antecedent. (2) בעל היכל הברכה: Heikhal ha-Berakhah is a book title, and 'בעל + title' is 'the author of' (cf. בעל חובת הלבבות); titles are transliterated, with the meaning in a note. (3) The וז"ל of 3:7.94 was dropped from the English though glossed; a stray space after the opening quotation mark is removed. Also: וכ' ע"ש read as וכו' (etc.) with ע"ש outside the quotation (see the token note); אף שמדבר is 'even though he speaks', not 'even one who speaks'; 'And the laws' is 'And among the laws'.

value: The paragraph is two quotations. The first is introduced by וז"ל המקובל בעל היכל הברכה (3:7.2-3:7.6), 'and these are the words of the Kabbalist, the author of Heikhal ha-Berakhah', and runs to וכו' (3:7.87); the author's own ע"ש (3:7.88) stands outside it. The words עולימתא שפירתא דלית בה עינין, ועינין דילה, תרין עטרין and בני נשא are Aramaic and are rendered by sense. The text does not name their source, and none is added.
מצות עשה על הב"ד לדרוש ולחקור: 'a positive commandment on the court to inquire and examine'. על with a noun reads 'incumbent upon'; the infinitives give the content of the commandment.
ואם כחשו זה לזה בטל העדות: a conditional with a perfect verb; the result clause is בטל, 'is void'. The two witnesses are the subject of the conflict (כחשו).
וז"ל followed by a name means 'and these are the words of X:', so the Kabbalist (3:7.3-3:7.6) is the speaker named by the formula and not part of the quotation. בעל + a book title is 'the author of'.
אף שמדבר אמת: אף ש is 'even though'; the clause is a concession to the main clause ויש עון גדול בזה, 'there is a great sin in this'.
The second quotation begins at כתב וז"ל (3:7.93-3:7.94) and ends at וכו' (3:7.129); the closing words והאריך עוד are the author's own report and take no quotation marks.
patches.reason: Corrects the first note and records the formula and the Aramaic words the first note missed.

patches.value: §8. And in the warning, "You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow," he wrote: "even standing by, to any degree. You shall not see your fellow's distress when one puts him to shame, and you are silent; they stood and answered no more. But you shall protest with all your power against him who disgraces your fellow, or speaks about him with talebearing and slander; you shall not be one who hears and is silent, but you shall say to him: 'Wicked one, troubler of Israel, why do you speak defiance against the likeness of our Maker, and against the Shekhinah of our strength, which is the yod in "among your people," and departs through this sin.' Therefore this was juxtaposed to that, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer,' and you might say: since I do not speak, I will listen and be silent, and take pleasure in what his fellow, a wicked man, speaks. This listener too is an utterly wicked person. And he transgresses 'You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow.' And he has no portion in the God of Israel when he hears a wicked one speak defiance against a righteous person, or whisper a whisper of lies about his fellow; rather, you shall immediately push him away and say to him: 'Wicked one, go away from me, I do not listen to you.' But if he hears and is silent, and all the more so if he takes pleasure, his end is to be judged in unblown fire, and he will not merit to stand in the company of the righteous, as listener, as answerer, as speaker. All of them shall perish from the world in this one, and in the world to come." Thus far his words.
patches.reason: (1) עמדו ולא ענו עוד: both verbs are third-person plural and the words are Job 32:16 (כי עמדו לא ענו עוד), 'they stood still, they answered no more'; 'he stood and did not answer again' is wrong (see the token note). (2) 'the Shekhinah, our strength' turns the construct שכינת עוזינו into an apposition: 'the Shekhinah of our strength'. (3) 'or whispers' makes the listener the whisperer; לוחש is parallel to מדבר under כששומע: 'or whisper'. (4) 'evil talk' for לשון הרע, against 'slander' in 3:7 and the token gloss. (5) 'evil talk, You shall not' is a comma splice with a capital; ועובר starts a sentence and needs 'And he'; ואין needs 'And'. (6) Style: 'that one puts him to shame' is ungrammatical English for שאחד מלבין פניו ('when one'); 'a listener and silent' is 'one who hears and is silent'; ותאמר is second person, 'and you might say'; 'the wicked one' is indefinite (רשע).

value: The quotation opens with כ' (he wrote) after the verse לא תעמוד על דם רעך, and closes at עכ"ל. Within it, direct address is in single marks, and the verse לא תעמוד על דם רעך is a single-marked quotation inside the outer quotation.
ולכך נסמכה זה לזה: 'for this reason this was placed next to that'. The verse לא תלך רכיל is the second member of the pair; ותאמר ('and you might say') begins the objection that the author answers.
עמדו ולא ענו עוד: both verbs are third-person plural, and the words are Job 32:16. 'They stood and answered no more' follows the verse; the Hebrew names no subject and none is added.

כששומע רשע מדבר סרה על צדיק, או לוחש מלחש בשקרים על חברו: לוחש is a participle parallel to מדבר, both governed by כששומע ('when he hears a wicked one speak ... or whisper ...'), so the wicked one is the whisperer.

וכל שכן ('all the more so') introduces the consequence. The three participles כשומע, כעונה, כמדבר ('as listener, as answerer, as speaker') are the ways of taking part, and כולם יספו ('all of them shall perish') refers back to them; for the other reading of the כ ('like'), see readings.
patches.reason: The first notes miss the Job verse that fixes עמדו ענו, and the parallel of לוחש with מדבר.

value: Lev 19:16: 'לא תעמוד על דם רעך' (3:8.2-3:8.7 and 3:8.90-3:8.96), and 'לא תלך רכיל' (3:8.71-3:8.73), quoted as the author gives them.
Lev 19:16, 'בעמיך', is the source of the yod of the Shekhinah (3:8.62-3:8.63); the author's reading, not a translation of the verse's sense.
Job 32:16: 'כי עמדו לא ענו עוד', 'they stood still, they answered no more' (3:8.23-3:8.26); the author's words are 'עמדו ולא ענו עוד'.
1 Kgs 18:17: 'עכר ישראל', 'troubler of Israel' (3:8.50-3:8.51); cf. Josh 7:25.
Job 20:26: 'אש לא נפח', 'a fire not fanned' (3:8.138-3:8.139); the author's printed word is נופח.
